title: 💻 Broadcom Patches 23 VMware Flaws — Three of Them Score 9.8 out of 10!
body: 💻 Broadcom Patches 23 VMware Flaws — Three of Them Score 9.8 out of 10!
Broadcom announced a major patch package for VMware products, fixing 23 security flaws, including 4 critical ones — three of them with a severity score of 9.8 out of 10, nearly the highest possible.

The most dangerous flaw is a new authentication bypass in the directory service of the vCenter platform, assigned CVE-2026-123903. It lets an attacker who can reach the network bypass login and access the system without a password.

The company itself confirmed that this flaw is completely different from a similar one it patched just 5 days earlier, CVE-2026-123890, which a spy group suspected of links to China has been exploiting since last September.

The other two critical flaws hit the Input/Output filtering service in the ESXi system and let an attacker who can reach the host run code directly on it, along with a fourth flaw scoring 9.3 in the virtual USB controller.

The package also includes fixes for Avi Load Balancer, Workstation, Fusion, and VMware Tools, with an important warning: fixes for the ESXi system version 9.0 are still pending, so anyone using it should restrict access to the management interfaces until the fix is released.
Broadcom mentioned no actual exploitation of these new flaws, but the history of the previous flaw is a reminder that attackers do not wait long.

Simply put: a single authentication-bypass flaw in vCenter could open every virtual machine it manages; the platform that runs everything is itself the most dangerous target, and updating it is not an option but a priority.
